text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: autopager triggered for gpu-host-17 (us-west1-rack4) — kubelet NotReady, agent-heartbeat lost, node not responding to /healthz. PD alert: PDINC-9012.

kai: acked. i'm on it, switching to oncall console.

charan: any kernel oops in the syslog?

marta: seeing serial console dropouts. tried to attach, console shows repeated 'hung task: kubelet' and then a stack trace. not a clean kernel panic but stuck in softlock.

dena: impact? any customer-facing load failovers?

kai: initial telemetry: ~0.6% of allocation attempts in us-west1 hitting placement failures while autoscaler retries — most requests fall back to other racks automatically. Dedicated customers unaffected. low-latency customers might see a handful of retries.

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty: Incident PDINC-9012 assigned to kai (on-call), escalation policy: infra-oncall -> infra-primaries.

kai: plan: 1) attach serial + get dmesg 2) attempt graceful cordon+drain if kubelet responds to control-plane 3) if serial console shows unresponsive kernel, hard reboot via IPMI and watch for repeated failure 4) if repeated kernel hangs, escalate to hw-rma.

charan: remote serial log snippet i pulled before it dropped:
```
[   45.234567] KERNEL_SOFTLOCKUP: CPU#3 stuck for 22s! [kubelet:1234]
[   45.234600] watchdog: BUG: soft lockup - CPU#3 stuck for 22s
[   45.234650] Call Trace:
[   45.234700]  <stack trace truncated>
```
seems like process-level deadlock, could be nvlink driver or kubelet thread.

marta: i'm trying kubectl get node gpu-host-17 -o wide but control-plane reports NotReady. kubelet not answering our healthz.

kai: ok cordon + prepare drain commands but don't drain until we confirm pods failover ok. run this in staging to verify first:
```
kubectl cordon gpu-host-17
kubectl drain gpu-host-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60
```

dena: i'm pinging our uptime dashboards and customer slack channels. sending a short note to SRE-notify with initial impact.

marta: tried a soft restart of kubelet via systemd over ssh but SSH to host is flaky. probably the hung kernel is affecting userspace.

kai: attach serial again and try to trigger a controlled reboot if possible. if serial accepts break, do:
```
ipmitool -I lanplus -H 10.10.4.17 -U admin -P **** chassis power cycle
```
only if we can't recover kubelet within 5m.

incident-bot: escalation policy will automatically escalate at 5m if node remains unacknowledged. Current status: acknowledged by kai.

charan: noticing repeated i/o errors on nvme in logs prior to softlock. marking as potential hw fault.

marta: ran a quick pod-impact check: 12 pods scheduled on the node, 3 stateful GPU pods with local disks. they'll need special handling; will flag team leads for those apps.

dena: messaging update sent to #customers-ops: "We're investigating a GPU host issue in us-west1; some allocation retries observed. We'll update in 30m or on milestone." :eyes:

kai: executing ipmi cycle now (serial showed kernel unresponsive for >2min). pasting output:
```
# ipmitool chassis power cycle
Chassis Power Control: Down/Up
```
reboot initiated, watching for console.

charan: putting node into quarantine in scheduler so new allocations avoid the rack until we confirm health: toggling placement policy for rack4.

marta: serial back; kernel shows reboot, bootloader starting. watching for kernel oops repeat.

kai: kernel booted to userspace, kubelet came up but then segfaulted after 90s. capturing coredump path and sending to infra-ml team for quick analysis.

dena: updating PD with current mitigation steps and estimated TTR 45m for deeper analysis + possible RMA.

charan: coredump stack indicates glibc abort in kubelet process around plugin unload. could be a driver race. I'll drop a patchback note to runtime team.

marta: re-scheduling the 3 stateful GPU pods onto other nodes with forced eviction where safe. doing one at a time.

kai: summary for now: node had a softlock/hung kubelet likely related to GPU driver/IO. autopager triggered correctly, node acknowledged, ipmi reboot recovered to a point but kubelet crashed on startup. next steps: collect full crash artifacts, move affected pods, prepare RMA for nvme/gpu if hw fault confirmed.

dena: customer comms queued for 45m if we don't have cleaner fix. tagging platform leads. :rotating_light:
